chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Nu'man Al-Ahowl, from Buraib Al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman on the condition that he teach her a chapter from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: 'I do not like that he should enter (consume) with her until he has taught her the chapter and given her something.' I said: 'Is it permissible if he gives her a date or a raisin?' He said: 'There is no problem with that if she is pleased with it, whatever it may be.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for consummating marriage when the dowry is teaching Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes that the teaching of a Quranic chapter serves as a valid dower (mahr), permitting the marriage to be consummated only after this instruction is completed and a gift is bestowed. He clarifies that the gift’s value is flexible, accepting even modest items like dates or raisins, provided the wife consents, thereby emphasizing the contractual nature of the dower and the importance of mutual satisfaction in Shia jurisprudence.
